newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian naphtha assessments hit four-year highs.
newsitem.headline: Asian naphtha assessments hit four-year highs.

text.p: Asian prompt physical naphtha price assessments hit four-year highs in Singapore and Japan on Friday on the back of firmer crude, traders said.
U.S./Iraq tensions have pushed Singapore naphtha price assessments for October cargoes to just below $21.90 a barrel ($197 a tonne) on Friday fob Singapore.
But levels had yet to reach the high assessments of $27.55 recorded in June 1992, traders said.
Japan's forward open-specification naphtha contract for first-half November, at $207/$208 a tonne, was similarly the highest level since June 1992.
"Prices have yet to reach Gulf war highs of around $240 (per tonne) in 1991," a trader said.
"Naphtha is underpriced ... it is cheap relative to crude," said a trader.
Traders said weak fundamentals have been keeping a cap on naphtha prices. In the absence of the Iraqi-factor, traders said they were bearish for naphtha prices.
Naphtha demand was moderated by turnarounds at petrochemical plants in north Asia in October and November, they said.
But because Asia was also relatively low to western markets in Europe, and the U.S. Gulf, prices will also find a floor.
"The East-West arbitrage has come in," said a trader who saw the East-West spread at around 50 cents.
"It only makes sense to take cargoes to the West. The market at the moment has found support," said a western trader.
